questions.stem: Which of the following structures is NOT part of the portal triad found in the liver?
questions.explanation: The portal triad consists of the hepatic artery, portal vein, and common bile duct. The hepatic duct is a separate structure that drains bile from the liver into the common bile duct.
questions.source: Basic hepatic anatomy; standard surgical teaching

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is part of the portal venous system?
questions.explanation: The portal venous system consists of veins draining the gastrointestinal tract to the liver. The splenic vein joins the superior mesenteric vein to form the portal vein. The hepatic artery and superior mesenteric artery are arterial, and the inferior vena cava is a systemic vein.

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man undergoes a laparotomy for a perforated duodenal ulcer. The surgeon wishes to identify the right gastroepiploic artery to ligate it safely. Which anatomical landmark best guides the location of this artery?
options: A. The posterior border of the pancreas
B. The anterior border of the transverse colon
C. The inferior border of the stomach
D. The superior border of the spleen
questions.explanation: The right gastroepiploic artery runs along the posterior border of the pancreas, supplying the greater curvature of the stomach. The other options describe borders unrelated to this vessel. Identifying the posterior pancreatic border allows safe ligation of the artery.
questions.source: Basic surgical anatomy of the stomach and pancreas

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a palpable, non‑tender mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑defined, encapsulated lesion arising from the splenic hilum. Which of the following structures is most likely involved in the origin of this tumour?
questions.explanation: The splenic hilum contains the splenic artery and vein, lymphatics, and nerves. A mass arising from the hilum most commonly originates from the splenic artery or vein. The pancreatic tail lies adjacent but is not part of the hilum, and the left adrenal gland is located superiorly. Therefore the splenic artery is the most likely source.

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a large, firm, non‑tender mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑defined lesion arising from the left hepatic lobe, with a central scar and peripheral enhancement. Which of the following anatomical features is most likely responsible for the lesion’s characteristic imaging appearance?
options: The presence of a fibrous capsule surrounding the lesion
The portal venous supply to the lesion
The arterial supply from the left hepatic artery
The biliary drainage via the left hepatic duct
questions.explanation: The classic imaging pattern of a focal nodular hyperplasia—a benign hepatic lesion—results from a fibrous capsule that surrounds the lesion and creates a central scar. This scar is visualised as a low‑density area on CT and a hyperintense area on MRI. The other options describe vascular or biliary anatomy that influence perfusion but do not produce the scar seen on imaging.
